recap.workouts:
No class and no lifting today — Sunday is bike only, and CMI4 is what landed. Nothing came through the phone log tonight, so this is read straight off the files.

The shape of the day: CMI4 was ridden as two pieces. Two hours indoors on Zwift carrying the entire interval content (load 153, 85% compliance against the paired plan), then the Zone 1 tail taken outdoors and extended — 1 hour 46 moving, 27.8 km, load 84. That is about 3 hours 46 of moving time and 237 load against a prescribed 3 hours and a planned 180. The intervals were completed and the easy tail was lengthened. That is the right way round, and it is worth saying so.

Indoors, segment by segment against the CMI4 prescription (20′ Z1 / 2 × [20′ Z3 / 15′ Z1] / 10 × [1′ Z4 / 2′ Z1]):
opener — 20:02 at 145 W, HR 128 average
Zone 3 block one — 20:00 at 224 W, HR entered at 137, peaked 166
Zone 1 — 16:19 at 134 W
Zone 3 block two — 20:00 at 224 W, HR entered at 135, peaked 168
Zone 1 — 15:02 at 139 W
Zone 4 — ten reps, every one at 274 W for about 58 seconds, recoveries 120–122 W

Every segment is where it should be and the band was never left: 224 W sits inside the 222–248 W Zone 3 band, 274 W inside 248–283 W for Zone 4. Honest about what that does and does not prove — on ERG the trainer holds the watts, so flat power is Zwift's work, not pacing skill. What you supplied was two hours on it without a single rep dropping.

The heart rate is where the information is, so read the peaks rather than the averages. Block one peaked 166, block two peaked 168 at identical power — two beats across forty minutes of threshold work, which is about as tightly coupled as this session gets. Recoveries did their job as well, back to the mid-130s before each block went off.

The Zone 4 set is the cleanest thing in the file. Rep peaks, in order: 159, 158, 158, 160, 161, 160, 159, 158, 158, 157. Thirty minutes, ten reps at 274 W, and the trend is flat to slightly down. On one-minute reps heart rate lags and lands in high Zone 3 with a brief spike, which is correct execution rather than a shortfall — watts were the sharp target there and the watts were exact ten times out of ten.

Outdoors: 1 hour 46 moving at 120 W average with HR averaging 128, which is honest Zone 1 against a 118–165 W band. One peak at 169, almost certainly a climb. It is one long unstructured lap so there is nothing to segment — easy end to end, and 45 minutes longer than the hour that was asked for.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps one-to-one onto CMI4's prescribed steps, not off auto-detected laps. The per-second pass was not available — the Drive folder again did not mount into the compute sandbox — so this is interval-level rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.
recap.takeaways:
1) The Zwift FTP check returned a DRIFT verdict tonight, and I am going to show you why I believe it is wrong, because acting on it would break something that is currently correct. Its words: "DRIFT: Zwift appears to have executed at FTP ~150 W, but the pipeline assumes 236 W (-36.3%). Fix Zwift's FTP to 236 W and decline its auto-detect prompt." Do not change anything yet. The report names its source as the OUTDOOR upload, not the Zwift ride, and it read that file's minutes 20–40 and 55–75 as though they were the two Zone 3 blocks — outdoors, on an easy tail, where you were turning about 148–150 W. Meanwhile the Zwift ride held 224 W in both Zone 3 blocks and 274 W in all ten Zone 4 reps. Those are 94.9% and 116% of 236, which is precisely where the bands sit at an FTP of 236. Zwift's FTP is fine. What needs fixing is the checker choosing between two activities that share a name on the same day.

2) The endurance verdict: executed, and executed well, with one thing on the watch list. Everything prescribed was delivered, and when the day ran long it was the easy tail that grew rather than the intervals that got firmed — the right trade and the plan's own preference. The watch item is heart rate against output. 224 W is 95% of FTP, and the peaks came in at 166 and 168, above the 159 threshold heart rate. On 28 July the CT31 block ran at 229.5 W — more power — with a 158.5 plateau and a maximum of 161. Today therefore cost more beats for less power. Before anything is read into that: this was the second and third hard blocks of a two-hour ride, not a standalone sixty-minute test, so it is not a like-for-like comparison and I would not call it a threshold move. Wednesday's CT31 is the clean read and it is three days out. Confidence: medium, interval-level rather than per-second.

3) ADAPT: no-op, and correctly so. CMI4 classifies as EXECUTED — full interval content, with the 85% compliance figure explained entirely by the tail leaving Zwift rather than by anything missing. Nothing in the remaining week moves. Tomorrow opens the deload, where nothing gets added, ever. RF12 stays absorbed from yesterday's call and is not owed.

4) Both of today's rides came in unrated. Rides are the standing gap in the load model — no Zwift session in the file carries a rating of your own, so the bike side of the comparison is built on nobody's scale. Two taps on the dashboard closes it.
recap.tomorrow:
Monday, and the deload starts. 06:00 class is 3-Position Clean, six singles on the 2:00 — take them at 75%, about 145, and the value is in the nine positional reps rather than the load. Then Town Policeman, four rounds on the 2:30 at [FITNESS] 95 lb: the barbell is only the buy-in to reach the erg, so move through it and ride the erg at a Zone 2 effort, not a sprint. Lifting is upper push and triceps at deload volume — incline dumbbell press 2 × 8–12 at 70, cable chest fly 2 × 12–15 at 40, lateral raise 2 × 15–20 at 20 (stay off the 25s this week), triceps pushdown 2 × 8–12 at 90. Load triggers are suspended all week. Endurance is CF3, thirty minutes: 5′ Zone 1, 20′ Zone 2 at 165–196 W, 5′ Zone 1, with the ten-minute reference block pinned at a fixed 165 W across minutes 5 to 15. That 165 does not move for anything — it is the whole point of the measurement.

Signals to read: whether the legs feel like they have just had nearly four hours of saddle time, whether 165 W in the first couple of minutes feels like nothing or like work, and whether the clean warm-up sets move freely.

Feeling good, legs willing? Take the complex at the top of the posted range, 80%, and hold the ten Zone 2 minutes after the block toward the upper part of the band. Legs heavy, or 165 W already feels like work? Complex at 75%, and hold those same ten Zone 2 minutes at the bottom of the band — 165 W, the same number as the block. Same thirty minutes either way, and both are a good day's work.

recapPrev.workouts:
Three pieces today, and the one that mattered was executed properly.

06:00 Cutthroat — 56' gym block, avg HR 112, max 151, load 20, RPE 5. You took 135 lb on the clean and jerks and normal wall walks rather than the light-bar [FITNESS] version I called for, plus the 60 single unders per round. Honest flag: on the lowest readiness morning of the block, that was the version with the most room to go wrong. It didn't — avg HR 112 and max 151 say you genuinely cruised it, and 21 total C&J reps at 135 sits well inside your strength. Noted, not scolded.

Arms and delts, the full Friday dose at exactly the deload loads: triceps pushdown 135 × 13, barbell curl 40 × 12, lateral raise 20 × 20. You were right about the Sorinex station — those are hamstring curls, so substituting your own barbell curls was the correct read, and the class banded face pulls covered the rear delts.

RAn4 — 45:03, 7.27 km, load 37 against a planned 45, RPE 5, paired cleanly to the planned session. The file splits exactly to the prescription: 15:01 warm-up, then 4 × (2:30 hard / 5:00 jog). Nothing missing, nothing added. The 82% compliance figure is intervals.icu scoring against its own preset zones, not a shortfall — every step is there at full length.

Warm-up: 5:56/km, HR 119 avg, max 132. Honest Z1.

The four reps, target band 3:48–4:17/km:
rep 1 — 4:08/km, HR 131 at the gun to 158 by the end
rep 2 — 4:03/km, 120 to 161
rep 3 — 4:08/km, 126 to 162
rep 4 — 4:03/km, 130 to 176

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (901 s warm-up, then 150 s / 300 s four times). The per-second stream pass wasn't available this evening — the Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox — so pace is per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.
recapPrev.takeaways:
1) The run verdict: clean. Four reps inside the pace band, five seconds per km of spread across the whole set, the last one tied fastest, HR shedding 50+ beats in every recovery, and no drift signal anywhere. Load 37 — a fraction of Thursday. As stimulus maintenance it did exactly its job, and there is no fatigue flag in the trace. Confidence: high on the pace read, medium on the HR read (per-rep peaks rather than per-second plateaus).

2) The call, straight. I recommended cutting RAn4 this morning at readiness 27 and you ran it — second day running that you overrode me and the file came back clean. What I actually think, rather than just conceding: the execution was good, and a load of 37 is not what turns a deload into Week 4 again. But two overrides in two days is a pattern worth naming, and the readiness signal — sleeping HR elevated a fifth straight morning, breathing now flagged too, Form −25.8 — still hasn't been paid for. One well-run session doesn't settle it. Tomorrow is where it gets settled.

3) ADAPT: no-op. RAn4 EXECUTED at full structure, Cutthroat done heavier than called but genuinely easy by HR, hypertrophy exact at the deload dose. Nothing in the remaining week moves — and on a deload nothing gets added, ever.

4) Lateral raise 20 lb × 20 tops the range: banked, not applied, per the deload rule. Week 9 now opens with lat pulldown to 190, face pull to 85, leg curl to 50, overhead triceps ext up one step, and lateral raise up one step. Five bumps waiting, all earned this week without spending them.

Everything else is clean — 7h40 asleep, 44 minutes deep, breathing 13.8, wrist temperature normal, no illness flag — so this reads as one large day rather than something going wrong, and the plan already answers it, because Monday of a deload week is thirty easy minutes and nothing else. One gap to name honestly: there is no sleep row for 23 August at all. Sunday's export never fired (no alarm, so the Shortcut never ran) and this morning's payload starts at midnight, carrying only the 00:39–04:34 tail of that night — not enough to log without inventing the first four hours, so it is left blank rather than written short. The only way today goes wrong is in the 06:00 hour: 3-Position Clean at 75%, about 145, and Town Policeman at [FITNESS] 95 lb with the erg ridden at a Zone 2 effort — the barbell is a buy-in to reach the erg, not the point. Town Policeman — on the 2:30 × 4 sets: [TRAIN] 12 power cleans 135/95 then max cal erg in the remaining time. [FITNESS]: 95/65.

On the metcon the barbell is not the point. It is a buy-in to reach the erg, and every second spent grinding 135 lb is a calorie not earned. Ride the erg at a Zone 2 effort, not a sprint.

Recovery, and it should feel almost pointless. Yesterday was 3h45 in the saddle with 50 minutes of hard riding in it. Thirty easy minutes is the whole job — no target to hit, no number to hold.

⚠ THE REFERENCE BLOCK WAS MOVED OFF THIS RIDE — to Saturday's CFF16. The first version of this plan put it here and post_week.py refused the entire week: "CF3 on 2026-08-24: no Z2 hold long enough for the 10-min reference block. Refusing rather than shortening or moving it." It was right. insert_ref_block requires the block to start at least 20 minutes into a session so the bin extractor's 15-minute warm-up exclusion cannot eat it — and CF3's Zone 2 hold ends at 25 minutes, so a block starting at 20:00 would run five minutes past it. CF3 cannot carry it, structurally.
And the argument used to put it here was wrong too. The claim was that CFF16 would push the block to minute 100 of a long ride and add cardiac drift. It does not — the block is pinned at minutes 20–30 whatever the ride's length, exactly where CF10's block sat on 10 and 17 August. Moving it preserves comparability rather than damaging it.

cf.desc:
7 rounds for time: [TRAIN] 200 m run + 12 alternating DB snatch 50/35 + 10 burpees over DB, rest 1:00 between rounds. [FITNESS]: 180 m run, 35/25, 8–10 burpees. Log total time to complete including rest.

Be clear what this is: 1400 m of running, 84 DB snatches and 70 burpees is a full aerobic session in its own right — and that is exactly why today has no endurance prescription at all. It is not a gap in the week; the aerobic work for Tuesday happens at 06:00.
The minute between rounds is what keeps this from becoming a 25-minute Zone X grind. Use it every round, including the early ones where it feels unnecessary. Zone X is the single easiest way to lose a deload week's ratio.
No lifting today either — the week's three upper days are Mon, Wed and Fri, and the leg session is Thursday.

end.name: CT31 — 60′ · BIKE THRESHOLD RETEST
end.detail: The block-boundary retest. tune.py analyses this automatically tonight and writes zones.json — it sets FTP and bike LTHR for weeks 13 to 21
end.desc:
5′ Zone 1 → 15′ Zone 2 @ 165–196 W → 24′ Zone 3 tune block @ 222–248 W → 11′ Zone 2 → 5′ Zone 1. (Verified library structure.)
This is the same session that set FTP 236 on 28 July, so the comparison is direct and like-for-like.
Set the effort in the first 3–4 minutes and then stop adjusting. One early correction, never a stair-step. tune.py reads steadiness as a coefficient of variation, and a sawtooth block reads as a dirty measurement even when the average is right.
Target the band and let heart rate tell the story. Last time the block averaged 229.5 W with the plateau at 158.5 against a bike LTHR of 159 — that is what a clean one looks like.
Do not ride it as a test of how much you can hurt. A block you fade out of measures your pacing, not your threshold. If heart rate is clearly under 159 at 24 minutes you have left something on the table — and that is the better of the two errors.
If today arrives genuinely flat, MOVE the retest to Thursday and drop RAn3. Do not water it down. A half-executed tune block costs full fatigue, produces a number anyway, and that number then sets nine weeks of zones.

cf.name: Captain Redbeard (time) — THE WEEK'S NON-NEGOTIABLE SCALE. [FITNESS], and step-overs all five rounds
cf.desc:
For time — descending row ladder, each row followed by 20 wall balls 20/14 and 20 box jump overs: 1000/900 m · 800/700 m · 600/500 m · 400/300 m · 200/150 m. [FITNESS]: 900/800 m start, wall balls 16/12.
Call: [FITNESS], and take the box jump overs as STEP-overs, all five rounds.
This is the week's one non-negotiable scale and the reason is specific. As written this is 3000 m of rowing, 100 wall balls and 100 box jump overs — roughly 200 reps of loaded squatting and jumping, plausibly the largest single leg-volume session of the entire week, sitting inside the deload, two days before the run retest.
Box jump OVERS are the expensive part. The landing is the eccentric cost, and step-overs remove nearly all of it for almost no loss of stimulus. If one thing in this week gets scaled, it is this, and it is worth more than any other adjustment available.
Row it steady and stop caring about the clock. Sunday's RT19 sets the run anchors for the whole Race-Specific block; there is no version of Friday that is worth more than that.

end.name: CFF16 — 150′ Z2 + 15′ Z3 finish · CARRIES THE 165 W REFERENCE BLOCK
end.detail: The week's aerobic ballast, and it now carries the week's most important measurement: 10 of the 130 Zone 2 minutes held at a fixed 165 W, placed automatically at minutes 20–30. The Zone 3 is at the END and there is no cool-down segment
end.desc:
5′ Zone 1 → 130′ Zone 2 @ 165–196 W → 15′ Zone 3 @ 222–248 W (fast finish). (Pulled live from the 80/20 library 23 Aug — CFF = fast finish. Do not read the 16 as short: CFF16 is 150 minutes, and the Zone 3 sits at the end with no cool-down listed.)
The 130 minutes are the session; the 15 are the seasoning.
Ride the Zone 2 in the band — 196 W is the ceiling and Zone X starts one watt later. On a ride this long the drift upward is unconscious rather than decided, which is exactly what makes it dangerous to the week's ratio.
The fast finish is 15 minutes at 222–248 W on two-hour legs, which is a genuinely different and more useful skill than the same fifteen minutes fresh. If the Zone 2 body was ridden too firm, do the finish anyway at the bottom of Zone 3 — do not compensate by making it harder.
Yes, this is a deload week and yes, this is a 150-minute ride. Both are true. It is the grid's own prescription for the row and the week's hours still fall 35.6%. Long easy volume is what a deload protects, not what it cuts.
If you are flat, ride the 130′ Zone 2 and skip the finish. Keep the volume, drop the intensity — never the reverse. That is the week's second cut, behind RAn3.

⚠ THIS RIDE NOW CARRIES THE 10′ @ 165 W REFERENCE BLOCK (moved here from Monday's CF3, which is structurally too short — the block must start 20 min into a session and CF3's Zone 2 ends at 25 min). Ten of the 130 Zone 2 minutes are held at a fixed 165 W, placed at minutes 20–30. It replaces Zone 2 rather than adding to it, so the ride is still 150 minutes. Regenerate with python make_zwo.py CFF16 --ref-block.
165 W is a fixed wattage, not a zone — it does not move when Wednesday's CT31 retunes FTP, and that is the entire point.
Three reasons this ride is actually the better home for it: the block lands at minutes 20–30 whatever the ride's length, which is exactly where CF10's sat on 10 and 17 August, so this is a like-for-like repeat; CFF16's own 15′ Zone 3 finish lets check_zwift_ftp.py measure the Zwift FTP offset from this same ride at age 0, instead of carrying a stale figure (stale carries dropped 4 observations from the verdict); and Saturday is 5 days clear of the 3h45 ride on the 23rd, so it inherits none of that fatigue.
Hold 165 W flat and do not chase it. Let heart rate say whatever it says — that reading is the measurement.
Why the weekend is this way round: this ride sits between Friday's metcon and Sunday's retest on purpose, because a steady ride does far less muscle damage the day before a run test than 100 box jump overs would.

end.name: RT19 — 90′ · RUN THRESHOLD RETEST
end.detail: The session that establishes the run anchors for the Race-Specific phase. tune.py analyses it automatically tonight and writes zones.json
end.desc:
5′ Zone 1 → 10′ Zone 2 @ 5:01–5:45/km → 20′ Zone 3 tune block @ 4:22–4:42/km → 50′ Zone 2 → 5′ Zone 1. (Verified library structure.)
Same code that measured your run anchors on 30 July, when 19.6 minutes at 4:27/km produced a heart-rate plateau of 167 with only +4.0 bpm of drift — the clean read that finally replaced the placeholder 162 copied off the bike.
Two things to get right. First, the 20′ block is threshold, not a time trial. 4:27/km is the reference and the band is 4:22–4:42. You said last time you could have held it about an hour — that is exactly the right feeling. Second, the 50 minutes afterwards must actually be Zone 2. Finishing the block and never coming back down is the classic error in this session and it is what turns a 90-minute run into an hour of Zone X.
Terrain note, settled 30 July: if you run this outdoors on rolling ground, the pace and heart-rate scatter that produces is terrain, not an execution fault — tune.py reads steadiness on a 30-second smoothed basis for exactly this reason. Run the effort, not the watch.
The honest caveat: this follows a 150-minute ride. If the block reads soft, that is a live alternative explanation to threshold down and it should be weighed before any anchor moves.
If today arrives genuinely flat, MOVE it into Monday of week 13 rather than watering it down. And per mandate §3 — deep soreness plus subjective slog on the Sunday of a deload week is your documented signature that the deload did not work. If today feels like that, that is information about the deload, not about your threshold, and it is a reason to move the retest rather than accept a low number.
